candidate_issue_snapshot.title: [SelectionDAG] memcmp/bcmp of 2^29+2 bytes is lowered to a 2-byte compare
[X86] Vector input for inline-asm constraint "A" asserts "lossy conversion of vector to scalar type"; missing diagnostic
candidate_issue_snapshot.body:
https://godbolt.org/z/K7n6Kn8h3 (`-O0`; `-O2` crashes the same way, x86_64)

```c
typedef long v2i64 __attribute__((vector_size(16)));
void f(v2i64 v) { asm("" : : "A"(v)); }
```
```
clang: llvm/lib/CodeGen/SelectionDAG/SelectionDAGBuilder.cpp:745: void getCopyToPartsVector(llvm::SelectionDAG&, const llvm::SDLoc&, llvm::SDValue, llvm::SDValue*, unsigned int, llvm::MVT, const llvm::Value*, std::optional<unsigned int>): Assertion `PartVT.getFixedSizeInBits() > ValueSize && "lossy conversion of vector to scalar type"' failed.
 #10 getCopyToParts(...) SelectionDAGBuilder.cpp
 #11 llvm::RegsForValue::getCopyToRegs(...) const
 #12 prepareDAGLevelOperands(...) SelectionDAGBuilder.cpp
 #13 llvm::SelectionDAGBuilder::visitInlineAsm(llvm::CallBase const&, llvm::BasicBlock const*)
```

The operand is invalid. GCC rejects it (`error: inconsistent operand constraints in an 'asm'`), and clang rejects the same vector as an `"=A"` output (https://godbolt.org/z/8e7ccTEac: `error: non-trivial scalar-to-vector conversion, possible invalid constraint for vector type`) and as an `"r"` input (`error: could not allocate input reg for constraint 'r'`). `"+A"` asserts the same way as `"A"`. A `__int128` in `"A"` works (`movq %rdi, %rax` / `movq %rsi, %rdx`).

Release builds give no diagnostic. They put only the low 64 bits of the vector in `rax` (`movq %xmm0, %rax`) and leave `rdx` unset (release trunk and GCC: https://godbolt.org/z/65fs1vd7j).

The same assertion from IR, with `llc -O0` or `-O2` (the `-O0` run is in the link above):

```llvm
target triple = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"

define void @f(<2 x i64> %v) {
  call void asm sideeffect "", "A"(<2 x i64> %v)
  ret void
}
```

#50251 was this assertion for a vector in `"r"`. Its fix, 81f6d7c, added `!VT.isVector()` guards to the GPR constraints (`r`, `q`, `Q`, `R`) in `X86TargetLowering::getRegForInlineAsmConstraint`. That is why `"r"` now gets the "could not allocate" error. `case 'A'` has no such guard: in 64-bit mode it returns `GR64_ADRegClass` for any type, so `getCopyToRegs` tries to fit the 128-bit vector into a single 64-bit part. There are two possible fixes: the same vector guard for `'A'`, or a diagnostic in `getCopyToPartsVector` like the one `getCopyFromPartsVector` already gives for outputs ("non-trivial scalar-to-vector conversion").

Found by a fuzzer (generated C program), reduced by hand.
Command: `clang --target=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -O0 -c repro.c` (same with `-O2`)
Tested: clang 24.0.0git ef45ca75ce72 (Compiler Explorer assertions trunk, 2026-09-29): the assertion above. Release trunk f4085066128a: exit 0, no diagnostic.
History: long-standing. Every assertions build I checked hits this assertion: 10.0, 12.0, 13.0, 16.0, 20.1, 23.1 and trunk. 3.9 also asserts in `getCopyToPartsVector`, with an older message ("Only trivial vector-to-scalar conversions should get here!"). The `"r"` variant still asserts in 12.0 and gets the error from 13.0 on. Not bisected.
Classification: crash on invalid code (GCC rejects it); release builds accept it without a diagnostic.
Related: #50251 (closed 2021): the same assertion with `"r"`, fixed by 81f6d7c. #173481 (open): the same assertion on AArch64 via llc. The X86 `'A'` handling here is separate target code, so it is not a duplicate. No open X86 issue found (searched "lossy conversion of vector to scalar type", `getCopyToPartsVector`).
